newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Strong team fights for Singapore telecom rights.
newsitem.headline: Strong team fights for Singapore telecom rights.

text.p: Telecom giants British Telecom (BT) and Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT) said on Thursday they joined a Singapore consortium to bid for the city-state's second basic telecommunications services licence.
The local partners in the consortium are government-owned Singapore Technologies Telemedia (STT), part of the Singapore Technologies group, and Singapore Power.
The consortium is the first to announce officially that it will be bidding for the second licence.
The Singapore government said earlier it would allow at least one and possibly two new operators to operate fixed line services by the year 2000.
Singapore Telecom has a monopoly in providing fixed line services in Singapore.
"This partnership brings together two of Singapore's strongest contenders for the bid as well as two of the world's largest and most successful telecommunications companies," an STT statement said.

Kapoor Gautam, regional telecom analyst with ING Baring Securities said: "It is a very strong consortium. Both BT and NTT are strong global players. On the other hand, Singapore Power offers the right of way (for telecom lines)".
Analysts said Singapore Power, which is the leading utility and energy group in the city-state, has an existing network of power lines which allows for easy laying of telecom lines.

"Having the power grid would make the consortium as good as any. BT and NTT will obviously bring the technical expertise for the telecom side," Timothy Wong, manager with Vickers Ballas Securities said.
Other major telecom companies are expected to announce their participation in the bidding for the licence over the coming weeks.
Analysts said they expect a consortium led by Keppel Telecommunications & Transportations Ltd and Singapore Press Holdings Ltd to announced their bid soon.
The Keppel consortium, together with Cable and Wireless already have the second mobile telephone and paging licence.
But the Keppel consortium have so far not announced who their foreign partners will be for the land licence.
